1	"""Claude's verdict on whether each product version is a coffee, stored in the lake.
2	
3	The rules (classify.py) measure about 94% on products labeled by hand; the long tail of things roasters sell next to
4	their beans (seeds, salt, rubs, canisters, oils, drinks) is more than rules can list. So every product version the
5	rules don't exclude outright is shown to Claude with the same written definition the labels were made against
6	(coffee_definition.md), and the answer is stored like any fetched fact. stg_products uses it when present, the rules
7	otherwise, so a build stays a pure function of the lake.
8	
9	Model: claude-haiku-5-5, chosen as the cheapest model at or above 98% on the validation set (eval/validation/).
10	Opt-in: nothing runs unless COFFEEDATA_VERDICT_MODEL names a model. Work is derived, not tracked: a product version
11	is pending when it has no verdict for this model and definition and isn't in an open batch.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import hashlib
17	import json
18	import logging
19	import os
20	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
21	from importlib import resources
22	from typing import cast
23	
24	from . import extract
25	from .classify import excluded
26	from .lake import Lake, new_batch_id
27	from .models import CatalogItem, Variant
28	
29	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
30	
31	DEFINITION = resources.files("coffeedata").joinpath("coffee_definition.md").read_text()
32	# Verdicts are kept per definition: changing the definition makes every product pending again.
33	DEFINITION_VERSION = hashlib.sha256(DEFINITION.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
34	LABELS = ("coffee", "not_coffee", "unsure")
35	SCHEMA = {
36	    "type": "object",
37	    "additionalProperties": False,
38	    "required": ["label"],
39	    "properties": {"label": {"type": "string", "enum": list(LABELS)}},
40	}
41	SYSTEM = (
42	    "You decide whether a product from a US coffee roaster's online store belongs in a catalog of coffees. "
43	    "Apply this definition exactly and answer with one label.\n\n" + DEFINITION
44	)
45	
46	# The same key stg_snapshots computes, so verdicts join to snapshots in dbt.
47	INPUT_HASH = (
48	    "md5(to_json(struct_pack(s.title, s.product_type, s.tags, s.body_hash, "
49	    "grams := list_transform(s.variants, lambda v: v.grams))))"
50	)
51	PENDING_SQL = """
52	with v as (
53	    select distinct on (input_hash) {input_hash} as input_hash, s.title, s.product_type, s.tags, s.body_hash,
54	           list_transform(s.variants, lambda v: v.grams) as grams
55	    from {snapshots} s
56	),
57	done as (select distinct input_hash from {verdicts} where model = $model and definition = $definition),
58	b as (select * from {verdict_batches} where model = $model and definition = $definition),
59	in_flight as (
60	    select distinct custom_id as input_hash from b where state = 'submitted'
61	      and batch_id not in (select batch_id from b where state = 'collected')
62	)
63	select v.*, bo.body_text
64	from v
65	left join (select body_hash, any_value(body_text) as body_text from {bodies} group by 1) bo using (body_hash)
66	anti join done using (input_hash)
67	anti join in_flight using (input_hash)
68	order by input_hash
69	"""
70	
71	
72	def model() -> str | None:
73	    return os.environ.get("COFFEEDATA_VERDICT_MODEL") or None
74	
75	
76	def item(r: dict) -> CatalogItem:
77	    return CatalogItem(
78	        roaster_id="",
79	        product_id="",
80	        handle="",
81	        url="",
82	        title=r["title"] or "",
83	        platform="",
84	        product_type=r["product_type"] or "",
85	        tags=r["tags"] or [],
86	        variants=[Variant(variant_id=str(i), grams=g) for i, g in enumerate(r["grams"] or [])],
87	        body_text=r.get("body_text") or "",
88	    )
89	
90	
91	def listing(it: CatalogItem) -> str:
92	    sizes = sorted({v.grams for v in it.variants if v.grams})
93	    return (
94	        f"Title: {it.title}\nProduct type: {it.product_type}\nTags: {', '.join(it.tags)}\n"
95	        f"Bag sizes (g): {', '.join(map(str, sizes)) or 'not stated'}\n\nDescription:\n{it.body_text[:1500]}"
96	    )
97	
98	
99	def request(it: CatalogItem, model_id: str, ttl: str = "5m") -> dict:
100	    """The definition is a fixed system prefix with a cache breakpoint, so every request after the first reads it
101	    from the prompt cache; only the listing is new input. Batches use a 1-hour TTL because a batch can take longer
102	    than five minutes to work through; one 2x write is shared by the whole batch."""
103	    return {
104	        "model": model_id,
105	        "max_tokens": 1024,
106	        "system": [{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": ttl}}],
107	        "output_config": {"effort": "low", "format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": SCHEMA}},
108	        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": listing(it)}],
109	    }
110	
111	
112	USAGE_FIELDS = ("input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "output_tokens")
113	
114	
115	def _add_usage(total: dict[str, int], msg: object) -> None:
116	    """Sum token usage, so a run's log shows whether the definition was read from the cache."""
117	    u = getattr(msg, "usage", None)
118	    for f in USAGE_FIELDS:
119	        total[f] = total.get(f, 0) + (getattr(u, f, 0) or 0)
120	
121	
122	def parse(msg: object) -> str | None:
123	    if getattr(msg, "stop_reason", None) in ("refusal", "max_tokens"):
124	        return None
125	    text = next((b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text"), "")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
126	    try:
127	        label = json.loads(text).get("label")
128	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
129	        return None
130	    return label if label in LABELS else None
131	
132	
133	def pending(lake: Lake, model_id: str, limit: int) -> list[dict]:
134	    sql = PENDING_SQL.format(
135	        input_hash=INPUT_HASH,
136	        **{t: lake.scan(t) for t in ("snapshots", "bodies", "verdicts", "verdict_batches")},
137	    )
138	    cur = lake.connect().execute(sql, {"model": model_id, "definition": DEFINITION_VERSION})
139	    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
140	    out = []
141	    for row in cur.fetchall():
142	        r = dict(zip(cols, row, strict=True))
143	        if not excluded(item(r)):
144	            out.append(r)
145	            if len(out) >= limit:
146	                break
147	    return out
148	
149	
150	# The Batches API takes at most 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch; each request repeats the definition and up
151	# to 1,500 characters of description (about 5 KB), so 10,000 keeps a batch near 50 MB.
152	BATCH_SIZE = 10_000
153	
154	
155	def submit(lake: Lake, limit: int = 100_000) -> dict:
156	    """Send pending product versions to Claude in Message Batches (half price; results within a day)."""
157	    import anthropic
158	    from anthropic.types.message_create_params import MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming
159	    from anthropic.types.messages.batch_create_params import Request
160	
161	    model_id = model()
162	    if not model_id:
163	        return {"skipped": "COFFEEDATA_VERDICT_MODEL is not set"}
164	    todo = pending(lake, model_id, limit)
165	    if not todo:
166	        return {"pending": 0}
167	    client = extract.client()
168	    out: dict = {"pending": len(todo), "submitted": 0, "batch_ids": []}
169	    for start in range(0, len(todo), BATCH_SIZE):
170	        chunk = todo[start : start + BATCH_SIZE]
171	        reqs = [
172	            Request(
173	                custom_id=r["input_hash"],
174	                params=cast(MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming, request(item(r), model_id, ttl="1h")),
175	            )
176	            for r in chunk
177	        ]
178	        try:
179	            batch = client.messages.batches.create(requests=reqs)
180	        except anthropic.APIError as e:
181	            log.warning("verdict batch submit failed: %s", e)
182	            out["error"] = str(e)
183	            break
184	        now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0)
185	        lake.write(
186	            "verdict_batches",
187	            f"verdict_batches/state=submitted/{batch.id}.parquet",
188	            [
189	                {"batch_id": batch.id, "state": "submitted", "at": now, "custom_id": r["input_hash"],
190	                 "model": model_id, "definition": DEFINITION_VERSION}
191	                for r in chunk
192	            ],
193	        )  # fmt: skip
194	        out["submitted"] += len(reqs)
195	        out["batch_ids"].append(batch.id)
196	    return out

199	def open_batch_ids(lake: Lake) -> set[str]:
200	    """Batches submitted but not yet collected."""
201	    vb = lake.scan("verdict_batches")
202	    return {
203	        r[0]
204	        for r in lake.connect()
205	        .execute(
206	            f"""select distinct batch_id from {vb} where state = 'submitted'
207	            and batch_id not in (select batch_id from {vb} where state = 'collected')"""
208	        )
209	        .fetchall()
210	    }
211	
212	
213	def collect(lake: Lake, run_date: str | None = None) -> dict:
214	    """Store the verdicts of finished batches, then mark each batch collected. Failed items stay pending."""
215	    import anthropic
216	
217	    con = lake.connect()
218	    open_batches = con.execute(
219	        f"""select distinct batch_id, model, definition from {lake.scan("verdict_batches")} where state = 'submitted'
220	        and batch_id not in (select batch_id from {lake.scan("verdict_batches")} where state = 'collected')"""
221	    ).fetchall()
222	    if not open_batches:
223	        return {"collected": 0}
224	    client = extract.client()
225	    run_date = run_date or date.today().isoformat()
226	    stored = 0
227	    usage: dict[str, int] = {}
228	    for batch_id, model_id, definition in open_batches:
229	        try:
230	            if client.messages.batches.retrieve(batch_id).processing_status != "ended":
231	                continue
232	            results = list(client.messages.batches.results(batch_id))
233	        except anthropic.APIError as e:
234	            log.warning("verdict batch %s: %s", batch_id, e)
235	            continue
236	        now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0)
237	        for res in results:
238	            if res.result.type == "succeeded":
239	                _add_usage(usage, res.result.message)
240	        rows = [
241	            {"decided_at": now, "input_hash": res.custom_id, "model": model_id, "definition": definition,
242	             "label": label}
243	            for res in results
244	            if res.result.type == "succeeded" and (label := parse(res.result.message))
245	        ]  # fmt: skip
246	        lake.write_partition("verdicts", run_date, new_batch_id(), rows)
247	        lake.write(
248	            "verdict_batches",
249	            f"verdict_batches/state=collected/{batch_id}.parquet",
250	            [
251	                {
252	                    "batch_id": batch_id,
253	                    "state": "collected",
254	                    "at": now,
255	                    "model": model_id,
256	                    "definition": definition,
257	                }
258	            ],
259	        )
260	        stored += len(rows)
261	    return {"collected": stored} | ({"usage": usage} if any(usage.values()) else {})
262	
263	
264	def judge(
265	    rows: list[dict], model_id: str, workers: int = 8, usage: dict[str, int] | None = None
266	) -> dict[int, bool]:
267	    """Synchronous verdicts for an evaluation set: {row index: is coffee}. Excluded rows and failed calls fall
268	    back to the rules, exactly as the build does. The first request runs alone so it writes the cache that the
269	    parallel ones then read; token usage is summed into `usage`."""
270	    import threading
271	    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
272	
273	    import anthropic
274	
275	    from .classify import is_coffee
276	
277	    client = extract.client()
278	    total = usage if usage is not None else {}
279	    lock = threading.Lock()
280	
281	    def one(i_r: tuple[int, dict]) -> tuple[int, bool]:
282	        i, r = i_r
283	        it = item(r)
284	        if excluded(it):
285	            return i, False
286	        try:
287	            msg = client.messages.create(**request(it, model_id))
288	            with lock:
289	                _add_usage(total, msg)
290	            label = parse(msg)
291	        except anthropic.APIError as e:
292	            log.warning("judge %d failed: %s", i, e)
293	            label = None
294	        return i, label == "coffee" if label in ("coffee", "not_coffee") else is_coffee(it)
295	
296	    indexed = list(enumerate(rows))
297	    first = next((k for k, (_, r) in enumerate(indexed) if not excluded(item(r))), None)
298	    out = dict([one(indexed.pop(first))]) if first is not None else {}
299	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(workers) as pool:
300	        out |= dict(pool.map(one, indexed))
301	    return out

66	def retail_only(cols: list[str]) -> str:

68	    people browse and pick from. A dim_coffee exported before is_wholesale existed (or a row from such a file read

73	def _load(lake: Lake | None = None) -> _Catalog:
74	    """The weekly dim_coffee export, read the way every query of it reads the files (union_by_name, so a column
75	    only some weeks' files have is there, null for the rest). Its columns, rows, index and wholesale set are read
76	    together and refreshed together, hourly, so a long-running MCP server picks up new catalog weeks and never
77	    pairs one week's columns with another's rows."""
78	    lake = lake or Lake()
79	    cached = _catalog_cache.get(lake.url)
80	    if cached and time.monotonic() < cached[0]:
81	        return cached[1]
82	    cat = _Catalog()
83	    try:
84	        src = ", ".join(f"'{s}'" for s in lake.mart_sources("dim_coffee"))
85	        con = lake.connect()
86	        scan = f"read_parquet([{src}], union_by_name = true)"
87	        cols = [r[0] for r in con.execute(f"describe select * from {scan}").fetchall()]
88	        stock = "in_stock" if "in_stock" in cols else "true"
89	        status = "catalog_status" if "catalog_status" in cols else "null"
90	        rows = [
91	            (
92	                cid,
93	                roaster or "",
94	                title or "",
95	                bool(retail),
96	                2 if state == "archived" else 0 if in_stock is not False else 1,

99	                f"select coffee_id, roaster_name, title, {retail_only(cols)}, {stock}, {status} from {scan}"

103	            cols,

107	            ok=True,
108	        )
109	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - no catalog yet just means no matches

115	def mart_columns(lake: Lake | None = None) -> list[str]:
116	    """The exported dim_coffee's columns: a remote read, so asked with the catalog's hourly refresh (they change
117	    only with the contract), not on every search. Raises if the read failed: a search without them would quietly
118	    show wholesale listings as retail."""

120	    if not cat.ok:

125	def _index(lake: Lake | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
126	    """coffee_id -> 'Roaster Name Coffee Title', from the weekly dim_coffee export."""

130	def _catalog(lake: Lake | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, str, str, bool, int]]:
131	    """(coffee_id, roaster_name, title, is_retail, rank) for every catalog coffee, wholesale listings included."""

135	def _tokens(s: str) -> list[str]:
136	    return [
137	        t for t in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", s.lower()) if len(t) > 1 and t not in {"coffee", "roasters", "co"}
138	    ]

141	CONFIDENT_SCORE = 80  # a match made without asking: 80+ and 5 clear of the next
142	CANDIDATE_SCORE = 50  # offered to pick from: about half the query's words found, or more
143	
144	
145	def match_score(query: str, label: str) -> int:
146	    """Mostly: what share of the query's words appear (fuzzily) in the label; WRatio breaks ties."""
147	    q, lab = _tokens(query), _tokens(label)
148	    if not q or not lab:
149	        return 0
150	    covered = sum(any(fuzz.ratio(a, b) >= 85 for b in lab) for a in q) / len(q)
151	    return round(70 * covered + 0.3 * fuzz.WRatio(query, label))

154	def owner_user_id() -> str:
155	    """The owner's user_id. Shots logged before accounts existed (user_id null) are the owner's."""
156	    return os.environ.get("COFFEEDATA_OWNER_ID") or "owner"

159	def fuzzy_match_coffee(text: str, limit: int | None = 3, lake: Lake | None = None) -> list[dict]:
160	    idx = _index(lake)
161	    if not text or not idx:
162	        return []
163	    # partial_token_set_ratio gives 100 to any title sharing one word with the text, so in a ~40k catalog its 300
164	    # are an arbitrary few of thousands of ties ("Finca El Puente - Honey Processed" lost to other roasters'
165	    # "Honey Process"). token_set_ratio's 300 are added: it ties far less on text that names a coffee, but short,
166	    # generic text ("Ethiopia Guji") still ties across many labels, so even this pool can miss the coffee meant.
167	    pool = {
168	        key: label
169	        for scorer in (fuzz.partial_token_set_ratio, fuzz.token_set_ratio)
170	        for label, _, key in process.extract(text, idx, scorer=scorer, limit=300)
171	    }
172	    scored = sorted(((match_score(text, label), key, label) for key, label in pool.items()), reverse=True)
173	    return [
174	        {"coffee_id": key, "label": label.strip(), "score": score} for score, key, label in scored[:limit]
175	    ]

178	def search_catalog(text: str, limit: int = 12, lake: Lake | None = None) -> list[dict]:
179	    """Coffees for a person to pick from: CANDIDATE_SCORE or better, ties sold now first as in match_bag, and no
180	    wholesale listings unless the text says wholesale (a twin outscores its retail coffee). Raises if the catalog
181	    couldn't be read, so a failed read isn't shown as no results."""
182	    mart_columns(lake)
183	    cat = _load(lake)
184	    skip = frozenset() if classify.says_wholesale(text) else cat.wholesale
185	    rank = {cid: r for cid, _, _, _, r in cat.rows}
186	    found = [
187	        m
188	        for m in fuzzy_match_coffee(text, limit=None, lake=lake)
189	        if m["score"] >= CANDIDATE_SCORE and m["coffee_id"] not in skip
190	    ]
191	    return sorted(found, key=lambda m: (-m["score"], rank.get(m["coffee_id"], 0), m["label"]))[:limit]

194	def _confident(ranked: list[dict], min_score: int) -> str | None:
195	    """The best candidate's coffee_id when it is 80+ and 5 clear of the next."""
196	    clear = len(ranked) < 2 or ranked[0]["score"] - ranked[1]["score"] >= 5
197	    return ranked[0]["coffee_id"] if ranked and ranked[0]["score"] >= min_score and clear else None

200	def _pick(said: str, ranked: list[dict], lake: Lake | None, min_score: int) -> tuple[str | None, list[dict]]:
201	    """The confident match among candidates ranked over the whole catalog, and the three to offer.
202	
203	    `said` is the coffee's own text. When it says wholesale ("Wholesale - 5LB Ethiopia Guji"), every listing
204	    competes. Otherwise retail coffees are tried first: a wholesale twin's title contains its retail coffee's, so
205	    it would tie with it and make the match unclear. The retail pick stands only if no wholesale listing outscores
206	    it (or ties with fewer words the text didn't say); then the whole catalog decides, so a coffee sold only as
207	    wholesale (or flagged wholesale only by a tag) is still matched from a bag that doesn't say so. Unclear: the
208	    wholesale listing that beats the retail candidates is offered first, then the retail candidates."""
209	    if classify.says_wholesale(said):
210	        return _confident(ranked, min_score), ranked[:3]
211	    wholesale = _load(lake).wholesale
212	    asked = set(_tokens(said))
213	
214	    def key(m: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
215	        # On a tie, the label with fewer words the text didn't say is the closer one: a twin "Wholesale - 5LB
216	        # Ethiopia Guji" adds words to "Ethiopia Guji", while a wholesale "Ethiopia Sidama" is closer to a bag
217	        # reading "Ethiopia Sidama" than the retail "Ethiopia Sidama Natural" is.
218	        return m["score"], -len(set(_tokens(m["label"])) - asked)
219	
220	    retail = [m for m in ranked if m["coffee_id"] not in wholesale]
221	    top = key(retail[0]) if retail else (-1, 0)
222	    above = [m for m in ranked if m["coffee_id"] in wholesale and key(m) > top]
223	    if not above and (best := _confident(retail, min_score)):
224	        return best, retail[:3]
225	    # Adding rivals can't make a retail coffee clear, so a match here is a wholesale listing.
226	    if best := _confident(ranked, min_score):
227	        return best, ranked[:3]
228	    return None, (above[:1] + retail + above[1:])[:3]

231	# --- logging -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
232	
233	_NUMBER = re.compile(r"(-?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(g|grams?|s|secs?|seconds?|°?c)?", re.I)
234	
235	
236	def _number(text: str) -> str:
237	    """'18.5 g' -> '18.5', '2,5' -> '2.5'. Anything else ('18-19', 'fine') is passed on as-is, so validation
238	    rejects it with a clear message instead of silently reading a different number."""
239	    m = _NUMBER.fullmatch(text)
240	    return m.group(1).replace(",", ".") if m else text
241	
242	
243	def _yes(value: object) -> bool:
244	    if isinstance(value, str):
245	        return value.strip().lower() in ("true", "yes", "y", "1", "x", "on", "milk")
246	    return bool(value)

249	def normalize(payload: dict) -> dict:
250	    out: dict = {}
251	    for k, v in payload.items():
252	        key = ALIASES.get(k.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_"), k.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_"))
253	        if isinstance(v, str):
254	            v = v.strip()
255	            if v in ("", "_No response_", "None"):
256	                continue
257	            if key in ("dose_g", "yield_g", "time_s", "grinder_setting", "water_temp_c"):
258	                v = _number(v)
259	            elif key in ("is_milk_drink", "deleted"):
260	                v = _yes(v)
261	        out[key] = v
262	    return out
263	
264	
265	def match_coffee(
266	    text: str, lake: Lake | None = None, min_score: int = CONFIDENT_SCORE
267	) -> tuple[str | None, list[dict]]:
268	    """The catalog coffee_id for free text, when the best match is confident and clearly ahead."""
269	    return _pick(text, fuzzy_match_coffee(text, limit=None, lake=lake), lake, min_score)
270	
271	
272	def match_bag(
273	    roaster: str | None, coffee: str | None, lake: Lake | None = None, min_score: int = CONFIDENT_SCORE
274	) -> tuple[str | None, list[dict]]:
275	    """Match what a bag's label says to the catalog, roaster first, then the coffee among that roaster's.
276	
277	    Reading the roaster separately is what the photo adds over typed text: a coffee name like "Hambela" is shared
278	    by dozens of roasters, but only one of them is on the bag. The roaster is matched by name (token set, so
279	    "Larkspur" finds "Larkspur Roasting Co."); its coffees are then scored on the name alone. With no roaster
280	    match the whole catalog is searched as for typed text. Same rule as typed text: confident only when the best
281	    match is 80+ and 5 clear of the next.
282	    """
283	    roaster, coffee = (roaster or "").strip(), (coffee or "").strip()
284	    rows = _catalog(lake)
285	    if not rows or not (roaster or coffee):
286	        return None, []
287	    roasters = {r for _, r, _, _, _ in rows if r}
288	    # Every roaster that scores 85+, not the top few: names that are token subsets of each other ("Onyx Coffee",
289	    # "Coffee Lab", "Onyx Coffee Lab") all score 100, and a cut-off could drop the real one.
290	    found = process.extract(roaster, roasters, scorer=fuzz.token_set_ratio, limit=None) if roaster else []
291	    near = [name for name, score, _ in found if score >= 85]
292	    if near and coffee:
293	        # Ties ("Finca El Puente" against four of one farm's lots) go to what's sold now.
294	        scored = sorted(
295	            ((match_score(coffee, t), rank, cid, f"{r} {t}") for cid, r, t, _, rank in rows if r in near),
296	            key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[3]),
297	        )
298	        matches: list[dict] = [
299	            {"coffee_id": cid, "label": label, "score": sc} for sc, _, cid, label in scored
300	        ]
301	    elif (
302	        near
303	    ):  # the roaster is clear but the coffee's name wasn't read: let the person pick, current lots first
304	        pick = sorted((rank, f"{r} {t}", cid) for cid, r, t, _, rank in rows if r in near)
305	        matches = [{"coffee_id": cid, "label": label, "score": 0} for _, label, cid in pick]
306	    else:
307	        matches = fuzzy_match_coffee(f"{roaster} {coffee}".strip(), limit=None, lake=lake)
308	    # Only the coffee's text says whether the bag is wholesale: a roaster's name can read as wholesale.
309	    return _pick(coffee, matches, lake, min_score)
310	
311	
312	def grinder_id(name: str, lake: Lake | None = None, user_id: str | None = None) -> str:
313	    """The equipment_id of the user's (default: the owner's) current grinder with this name."""
314	    user_id = user_id or owner_user_id()
315	    grinders = [
316	        e
317	        for e in (lake or Lake()).latest("equipment", "equipment_id")
318	        if e["kind"] == "grinder" and (e["user_id"] or owner_user_id()) == user_id
319	    ]
320	    # A retired grinder only if no current one has the name; among several, the most recently changed.
321	    named = [e for e in grinders if (e["name"] or "").strip().lower() == name.strip().lower()]
322	    for e in sorted(named, key=lambda e: (not e["retired"], e["logged_at"]), reverse=True):
323	        return e["equipment_id"]
324	    known = ", ".join(sorted(e["name"] for e in grinders if not e["retired"])) or "none yet"
325	    raise ValueError(f"no grinder named {name!r} (known: {known})")
326	
327	
328	def record(shot: Shot, lake: Lake, deleted: bool = False, after: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
329	    """Write one shot record. `after` is the shot's previous logged_at: the new record must sort after it
330	    (logged_at has whole seconds). The file name also carries a random suffix, so two records in the same
331	    second never collide."""
332	    now = datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0)
333	    if after and now <= after:
334	        now = after + timedelta(seconds=1)
335	    lake.write(
336	        "shots",
337	        f"shots/{shot.shot_id}__{now:%Y%m%dT%H%M%S}-{secrets.token_hex(3)}.parquet",
338	        [shot.model_dump() | {"logged_at": now, "deleted": deleted}],
339	    )
340	    return now
341	
342	
343	def last_logged(shot_id: str, lake: Lake) -> datetime | None:
344	    """When this shot was last recorded, from its own files only (one glob), so a correction sorts after it."""
345	    con = lake.connect()
346	    found = []
347	    for src in lake.sources("shots"):  # staging, then the remote lake: each may have none
348	        glob = f"{src.rsplit('/', 1)[0]}/{shot_id}__*.parquet"
349	        try:
350	            row = con.execute(
351	                f"select max(logged_at) from read_parquet('{glob}', union_by_name = true)"
352	            ).fetchone()
353	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - duckdb.IOException: no file for this shot there
354	            continue
355	        if row and row[0]:
356	            found.append(row[0])
357	    return max(found, default=None)
358	
359	
360	def log_shot(
361	    payload: dict, lake: Lake | None = None, min_score: int = CONFIDENT_SCORE
362	) -> tuple[Shot, list[dict]]:
363	    """Validate and record a shot as its own immutable lake file. Free-text coffee is matched to the catalog.
364	    To correct a shot, log it again with the same shot_id (latest wins); add deleted=True to retract it."""
365	    lake = lake or Lake()
366	    data = normalize(payload)
367	    deleted = _yes(data.pop("deleted", False))
368	    data.setdefault("shot_id", str(uuid.uuid4()))
369	    data.setdefault("brewed_at", datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"))
370	    if name := data.pop("grinder_name", None):
371	        data["grinder_id"] = grinder_id(name, lake)
372	    matches: list[dict] = []
373	    if not data.get("coffee_id") and data.get("coffee_freetext"):
374	        data["coffee_id"], matches = match_coffee(data["coffee_freetext"], lake, min_score)
375	    shot = Shot(**data)
376	    # A correction (an explicit shot_id) must sort after the record it corrects, even within the same second.
377	    record(

Old shot files don't have these columns. The lake is read with `union_by_name = true`, so they come back as null,
and nothing about an old shot changes. `Shot` in `models.py` gains the same optional fields; it has
`extra = "forbid"`, so this has to land before the app sends them. The MCP `log_shot` tool gains an
optional `grinder_name` argument that resolves to an `equipment_id` by name. (Not `grinder`: `shots.ALIASES`
already maps `grinder` to `grinder_setting`.)

A grind setting is now only comparable within one grinder, so `mart_dial_in` groups by user, coffee and
`grinder_id`, treating null as "the grinder used before equipment existed". `suggest_next` doesn't change: the app
doesn't use it, and it keeps serving the MCP server and the issue-form replies as it does today.

### dbt changes

- `stg_equipment`, `stg_bags`: latest record per id, without deleted ones, the same shape as `stg_shots`. Photos are
  not modelled in dbt; the server reads them directly from the photo dataset.
- `dim_equipment`: current equipment.
----
- Passwords never leave the server in plain text and are never logged. Request logging drops the body of the
  sign-in, sign-up and reset routes.
- The image goes to the Anthropic API to be read. Under standard API terms it isn't used for training; it is still
  a third party seeing a photo of a kitchen counter. The capture screen frames the bag tightly to keep the
  background small.
- Shots leave the public site. Today `site.py` renders "My shots: rating by brew ratio" and "Recent shots" from
  `fct_shot` on the GitHub Pages site; milestone 1 removes both sections and the scatter chart, and adds a test
  that the generated site contains no shot fields. Shots are then visible only in the app.
- The "Log a shot" issue form posts the shot and the reply as a GitHub issue, which is public if the repo is. #15
  kept it, since `suggest_next` still serves its replies. It stays until the app is live; then it comes off `main` and
  is kept on an archive branch, never deleted.

## Cost

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
----

The app doesn't suggest grind changes. The current rule ("sour or fast, go finer") is a rule of thumb, not something
learned from these shots, and a confident-looking suggestion from it would be wrong often enough to mislead. The
data the app collects is what a better suggestion needs: grind, dose, yield, time, taste, rating, grinder and the
bag's roast date.

Once a coffee has enough shots on one grinder (about 20), fit a small per-bag model of time and taste against grind,
dose and days off roast; a regression with a term per bag is enough to start. Compare it with the rule of thumb on
held-out shots: for each held-out shot, which one better predicted the time and taste of the next one? Show a
suggestion in the app only when the model reports its confidence and beats the rule of thumb on that test, and say
how sure it is ("Try 11. Likely 26 to 30 s.") instead of stating a single answer.

`shots.suggest_next` stays as it is for the MCP server and the issue-form replies.

## Decisions (October 27)

| Question | Answer | What it changes |

| Phone | Android | Haptics work through `navigator.vibrate`. The PWA installs from Chrome and keeps its login like a normal tab. Web Bluetooth is available if a scale is wanted later. |

| Photos | Stay private, still Parquet, in Hugging Face's image layout | Separate private dataset, one photo per Parquet file, the `image` column as `struct<bytes, path>` with the `Image` feature metadata. One write path, and the photo and its metadata stay together in one immutable file; plain JPEGs would need a separate metadata table kept in step. |
| Grind suggestions | Deferred until there's a model trained on the owner's shots | The app describes each shot and suggests nothing. `shots.suggest_next` stays for the MCP and issue-form replies. See Later: a dial-in model. |
| Shot timer | Built in, but typing must also work | The time row has Start/Stop and Type side by side. |
| Rating default | Empty, with a way to say "same as last" | Taste and rating start empty; a "Same as last" chip fills both. |
| Other users | The owner plus people they invite; nobody else uses the owner's machine | Invite-only sign-up, per-user data, a `user_id` on every personal record. |

# Findings 01: can the app say what to change after a shot, like the CLI?

Commit: `6bda240` (HEAD of `main`). I changed no code.

## Short answer

The app doesn't do this today, and that was decided on purpose. The CLI, the MCP server and the issue-form replies
all call `shots.suggest_next`, a fixed rule of thumb (no Claude call) that says "go finer to X" or "go coarser to
X". The app's screens describe the shot instead ("Inside the window, two seconds slower than Monday's shot.").
There is a test that fails if the words "finer", "coarser" or "Try N" ever appear on those screens. The plan holds
grind suggestions back until a dial-in model, trained on the owner's own shots, beats the rule of thumb on held-out
shots.

## 1. What the CLI does after a shot

- **Command:** `coffeedata shot add --json '{...}'`, or `coffeedata shot from-issue [--file body.md]`, which
  reads a GitHub issue-form body. See `src/coffeedata/cli.py:408-418` (`cmd_shot`) and `cli.py:634-637` (argparse).
- **Flow:** `shots.log_shot()` checks the shot and writes it to the lake, then `lake.publish()`, then it prints
  `shots.issue_reply()`. That reply is "Logged shot …", the catalog match line, and
  `shots.suggest_next(coffee_id or coffee_freetext)` (`src/coffeedata/shots.py:497-508`).
- **Inputs it accepts** (`shots.ALIASES`, `shots.py:28-43`): dose/in, yield/out, time, grind, taste
  (sour/balanced/bitter), rating, coffee/bean, temp, method, milk, grinder_name.
- **The advice logic** is `suggest_next` in `src/coffeedata/shots.py:412-463`. It is a **fixed heuristic with no
  Claude or LLM call**:
  - It takes the coffee's shot history (`history()`: exact `coffee_id`, otherwise fuzzy free text with WRatio ≥ 85)
    and looks at the last shot.
  - Targets: `TARGET_RATIO = (1.8, 2.3)` and `TARGET_TIME = (25, 32)` s (`shots.py:24-25`).
  - The step is the smallest gap between grind settings used so far, else 1.0 (`_step`). Which way is finer comes
    from the grinder's `finer_is_lower` in equipment; if that isn't set, lower is finer.
  - The rules, in order:
    1. Sour, or no taste given and faster than 25 s: go finer by one step.
    2. Bitter, or no taste given and slower than 32 s: go coarser by one step.
    3. Balanced but outside the time window: keep the grind, or move it to bring the time back.
    4. Time fine but ratio outside 1.8 to 2.3: pull to about 2× the dose.
    5. Otherwise: "That's in the window".
  - It adds the best-rated shot of this coffee when there is more than one shot.
  - With no shots it gives a starting recipe.
- The same function is also an MCP tool (`src/coffeedata/mcp_server.py:110-113`), and `log_shot` over MCP returns
  `issue_reply` (`mcp_server.py:45`).

**Evidence, a run of the real CLI against a throwaway local lake** (`COFFEEDATA_LAKE=$(mktemp -d)/lake`, no
catalog, so there was no coffee match):

```
$ coffeedata shot add --json '{"coffee_freetext":"Test Bean","dose":18,"yield":36,"time":21,"grind":15,"rating":3,...}'
Logged shot `f4159772-…`.
Last shot: 18 g → 36 g (1:2.0) in 21 s at grind 15. It ran fast (21 s): go finer to 14 to slow the shot and extract more.

$ coffeedata shot add --json '{... "time":35,"grind":14.5,"rating":2,"taste":"bitter" ...}'
Logged shot `3d5445bf-…`.
Last shot: 18 g → 36 g (1:2.0) in 35 s at grind 14.5. It tasted bitter: go coarser to 15. Your best-rated shot of this coffee (3/5): grind 15, 18 g → 36 g in 21 s.
```

## 2. Does the app show such advice today? No, by design

What the app shows after a shot:
- `app/views.py:1-2`, the module docstring: "Descriptions only; the app doesn't suggest a grind change (PLAN,
  'Later: a dial-in model')."
- `views.summary()` (`app/views.py:67-80`) says whether the time was fast, slow or in the window, and compares it
  with the previous shot. Its own docstring says "What happened, not what to change."
- The app imports only the constants `TARGET_RATIO` and `TARGET_TIME` from `coffeedata.shots`
  (`app/views.py:12`). Nothing under `app/` calls `suggest_next`; I grepped the whole repo for `suggest_next` and
  `issue_reply`.
- The Saved screen (`app/templates/saved.html`) and Today (`app/templates/today.html:21-22`) show the time-by-ratio
  target chart, the summary (in a `.advice`-styled paragraph, but describing the shot only) and the bag's shot
  sequence.
- The Log form's prefill (`app/store.py` `prefill`, around lines 222-298) copies the last shot's grind. If there is
  no shot on that grinder yet it starts mid-dial, with a comment: "a starting point to move from, not advice."
- When a shot is saved offline, `app/static/app.js:473` describes the shot from the form alone ("no server logic
  copied here").

What it doesn't show, and the docs and tests that say so:
- `docs/app/PLAN.md:674` (Decisions table): "Grind suggestions | Deferred until there's a model trained on the
  owner's shots | The app describes each shot and suggests nothing. `shots.suggest_next` stays for the MCP and
  issue-form replies."
- `docs/app/PLAN.md:649-662` ("Later: a dial-in model"): the rule of thumb "would be wrong often enough to
  mislead". The plan is a per-bag regression once about 20 shots exist on one grinder. It is compared with the rule
  of thumb on held-out shots and shown only if it wins, and it states its confidence ("Try 11. Likely 26 to
  30 s.").
- `docs/app/DESIGN.md:69, 128, 387`: 'No "go finer" or "try 11" until the dial-in model in the plan exists.'
- `tests/test_app.py:124-136` (`test_save_shows_saved_and_today_without_grind_advice`) checks that Saved, Today
  and Log contain no `finer|coarser|Try \d`. `tests/browser/app_flow.js:117` checks the same in the browser.

Tests I ran:
```
$ uv run --offline pytest -q tests/test_shots.py::test_suggest_next \
    tests/test_app.py::test_save_shows_saved_and_today_without_grind_advice
2 passed
```
The first covers the CLI and MCP advice; the second checks that the app has no advice.

## 3. What porting it to the app would touch

**Shared logic is possible; it wouldn't need rewriting.**
- `suggest_next` is plain Python in the `coffeedata` package, which the app already imports (`app/views.py:11-12`).
- It doesn't fit the app's data as it stands:
  - It reads shots from the lake by `coffee_id` or fuzzy free text with `load_shots`, across **all users**. There
    is no `user_id` filter in `history()` or `load_shots()`.
  - The app keeps per-user shots in memory in `app/store.py` (`shots_of(user_id)`, `bag_shots`,
    `coffee_shots`).
  - The app groups by bag and grinder. PLAN.md:532 says grind settings only compare within one grinder;
    `suggest_next`'s `_step` and best-shot both mix grinders.
- A port would most likely factor the rule into a pure function over a list of `Shot`s plus a grinder, and call it
  from both `suggest_next` and the app. A direct call would show other users' shots and mix grinders. I haven't
  verified that a refactor keeps the MCP and issue output byte-for-byte; the tests above would cover part of it.

**Backend / API**
- `app/main.py` `saved()` (around line 616) and `today()` (around line 461) would compute the advice next to
  `views.summary(...)` and pass it to the template.
- I found no separate JSON endpoint for the summary; the pages are rendered on the server. Offline saves
  (`app.js:473`) would show no advice until sync, unless the rule were copied into JS. The file's comment argues
  against that.

**UI**
- `app/templates/saved.html` and `today.html`, which already have the `.advice` serif slot.
- Possibly the Log form's grind prefill (`store.prefill`). DESIGN.md:69 discusses whether advice should
  apply itself and calls the question moot for now.

**Tests and docs that would have to change, since they encode the current decision**
- `tests/test_app.py:134`, `tests/browser/app_flow.js:117`.
- PLAN.md Decisions row and "Later" section, DESIGN.md Copy section (line 387) and line 69.
- Reversing these is the owner's product decision. The investigation can't settle it.

**Would the CLAUDE.md eval rules apply?** Very likely yes, in full.
- CLAUDE.md covers "any change whose quality is 'how often is it right'", heuristics included. Showing grind advice
  in the app is a change to how users get a rule's decision: every app shot would start showing output it doesn't
  show today. Step 9's 50-product shortcut is counted in products whose output changed and fits a catalog field
  poorly. Either way, "a change to how a rule decides" needs the full process.
- PLAN.md already names the evaluation it wants: held-out shots, the rule of thumb against a model, shown only if
  it wins and states its confidence.
- Showing today's `suggest_next` unchanged (no new rule) is ambiguous under CLAUDE.md:
  - The rule itself wouldn't change.
  - Its audience would, and the owner's recorded reason for holding it back is that it's wrong too often.
  - I'd treat it as needing at least a measurement of how often the rule is right, on held-out shots split by
    coffee/bag (the analogue of grouping by roaster). The owner should make that call.
- There is no existing eval for shot advice under `eval/`. `eval/sealed/` is for the coffee classifier.
  `app/eval/bag_read.py` is for bag-photo reading.

## What I didn't check / couldn't determine

- I didn't read `app/main.py` in full: only the `today`/`saved` call sites and grep hits. There may be other
  screens (e.g. bag or coffee pages) that show summaries.
- I didn't run the full test suite or the browser test (`tests/browser/app_flow.js`), only the two tests above.
- I didn't look at the real lake (`$COFFEEDATA_LAKE` remote, HF). So I don't know how many shots the owner has or
  how often `suggest_next` is right on them, and I can't say whether any coffee has reached the ~20-shots-per-grinder
  threshold.
- I didn't check the mockups or screenshots in `docs/app/mockups` and `docs/app/screenshots` for advice UI.
- I didn't check `dbt` `mart_dial_in` beyond the PLAN references.
- I didn't check whether `lake.publish()` on a local (non-`hf://`) lake does anything beyond local staging. The
  CLI run used a temp directory and no remote credentials were involved as far as I could see, but I didn't
  verify that by reading `publish` in full.
- Whether the owner wants to reverse the deferral can't be found in the code. It is a product decision.
